title: Site Observability — Carrier-AMER
description: Country > Site > Device drill-down for Carrier-AMER. site_id is derived from the device hostname (AT-7689-ASW01 -> AT-7689) and country from its ISO prefix.

panels.title: Sites in $country
panels.description: Every site whose hostname prefix maps to this country. Sort by Down to find problem sites.

panels.title: Device availability — $site
panels.description: Polled every 5 minutes, which is also how often Meraki refreshes this data. Shorter outages are not visible.

panels.title: WAN utilisation — $site
panels.description: site_id here comes from capacity.yml. If this is empty while devices show, capacity.yml site_id does not match the hostname convention.

panels.title: Channel utilisation by band — $site
panels.description: High WiFi utilisation means you need capacity. High non-WiFi means interference, and adding APs will not help.

panels.title: Memory utilisation — $device
panels.description: Available for every Meraki device type.

panels.title: CPU load average — $device
panels.description: ACCESS POINTS ONLY. Meraki exposes no CPU metric for MS switches or MX appliances, so this is empty for those. It is a load average, not a percentage.

panels.title: Switch ports & PoE — $device
panels.description: Switches only. Aggregated per switch rather than per port -- per-port series across this estate would be six figures of cardinality.

panels.title: API request rate — this org
panels.description: Meraki allows 10 req/s per ORGANISATION. Tiered polling keeps the average far below the cap; brief peaks during the 15-minute switch sweep are expected.
